prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity desktop personal website mockup for Aaron Cassar, edge-to-edge at 1440 by 1000 landscape, no browser frame. It is radically minimal, incredibly polished, coder-like. This concept is an open source note: a compact text-only personal introduction positioned in the upper-left quadrant of a mostly empty cool-white page, with very generous page margins. IBM Plex Mono-like regular text, blue-black ink, restrained steel gray secondary text. Real content: 'Aaron Cassar' as a small name heading. Under it, 'Software engineer. Curious by default.' Then a concise paragraph 'I build software, make worlds, and occasionally go outside.' A row of quiet text links 'Selected work ↗' and 'Get in touch ↗'. A second separate block much lower: a small terminal command styled as an interactive text button '→ open terminal', under it a tiny line 'A few things are hiding in here.' In the bottom margin a sparse single line of links 'GitHub   LinkedIn   Résumé'. Upper right a tiny sun-outline theme switch. No header bar, giant typography, cards, illustrations, imagery, gradients, grid backgrounds, borders or logo. The page feels like one carefully composed plain-text file, but with unusually beautiful spacing and optical alignment. Everything is readable and modest in scale, and 80 percent of the screen remains empty. Small dark terminal cursor is the only playful element. Calm, informal, personal, and uncompromisingly simple. The secret terminal is a discovery behind this sparse first surface.
